questions.learningObjective: Compute rows removed by key deduplication
questions.stem: A memo table has 70 rows and 66 distinct keys. How many rows are removed by keeping one row per key?
questions.explanation: 70 rows minus 66 distinct keys leaves 4 extra rows removed.
questions.hint: Subtract distinct keys from total rows.

questions.subject: DATA_SCIENCE
questions.topic: A trimmed mean
questions.learningObjective: Compute a trimmed mean
questions.stem: A memo lists 1, 3, 5, 7, 9, 11, 100. Trimming the top and bottom 14% (one value each), what is the trimmed mean?
questions.explanation: Removing 1 and 100 leaves 3,5,7,9,11; their mean is 35/5 = 7.
questions.hint: Drop one from each end then average.

questions.subject: DATA_SCIENCE
questions.topic: Reading a standardised value
questions.learningObjective: Compute the original value from a z-score
questions.stem: A memo reports a mean of 100 and standard deviation of 10. A fact has z-score 2.0. What is its original value?
questions.explanation: Original value = 100 + 2.0*10 = 120.
questions.hint: Multiply z by standard deviation and add the mean.

questions.subject: DATA_SCIENCE
questions.topic: The value mean imputation writes
questions.learningObjective: Identify a property of mean imputation
questions.stem: Mean imputation in a memo's column has which effect on the mean?

options.text: It increases the mean.
It decreases the mean.
It makes the mean undefined.
It leaves the mean unchanged.

questions.explanation: Mean imputation fills missing cells with the observed mean, so the overall mean stays unchanged.
questions.hint: The fill equals the observed mean.

questions.subject: DATA_SCIENCE
questions.topic: How far the median fill sits below the mean
questions.learningObjective: Identify when the median fill sits below the mean
questions.stem: In a memo's left-skewed column, where does the median fill sit relative to the mean?

options.text: Above the mean, because skew pulls the mean down.
Below the mean, because skew pulls the mean down.
Equal to the mean, because both are central.
At zero, because skew eliminates the median.

questions.explanation: Left skew pulls the mean downward, so the median fill sits above the mean.
questions.hint: Left skew pulls the mean down.

questions.subject: DATA_SCIENCE
questions.topic: The share a mode fill creates
questions.learningObjective: Identify the effect of mode imputation on diversity
questions.stem: Mode imputation in a memo's category column has which effect on diversity?

options.text: It increases diversity by adding new categories.
options.misconception: reverses the effect of mode imputation

options.text: It removes all categories.
It preserves diversity exactly.
It decreases diversity by repeating one category.

questions.explanation: Mode imputation reduces diversity by filling missing entries with one repeated category.
questions.hint: Every missing slot becomes the mode.

questions.subject: DATA_SCIENCE
questions.topic: Reading a standardised value
questions.learningObjective: Summarise what a z-score means
questions.stem: A memo reports a z-score of 0. Stage one: where is the value relative to the mean? Stage two: what does that imply?

options.text: The value is at the mean; it is exactly average.
The value is one standard deviation above the mean.
The value is one standard deviation below the mean.
The value is zero; it must be missing.

questions.explanation: A z-score of 0 means the value equals the mean, so it is exactly average.
questions.hint: Zero z means at the mean.
